It does matter because each animal is treated differently and I wanted to give you insight on the farming practices of said animals. In the case of chickens it's really simple. Fertilized eggs have a 50/50 chance of being either male or female. If you think about it, that means that (statistically) all the chickens in your neighbor's back yard are only half of the birthed ones. That means something happened to the other half. Standard farming practice is to kill them. It's what's called chick culling. These practices include:

  • Maceration, using a large high-speed grinder into which the live chicks are fed.
  • Gases or gas mixtures, often carbon dioxide is used to induce unconsciousness and then death.
  • Cervical dislocation (breaking the neck)
  • Electrocution, a new method that has been touted as being cheap, reliable, and humane by its developers (though there's no active source on this)
  • Suffocation in plastic bags

The most common of which is Maceration.

You'll find that different vegans have different stances on all of these issues, but I'll try to give you my stance and explain the reasoning behind them one by one.

  • Laying hens - Absolute no. This is simple, like I said before, laying hens come with a price - one out of two times when an egg hatches, it's a male. Male chicks have no use in the laying industry (industry meaning even someone's backyard - it's a business). They're not profitable. You can either raise them for meat, or kill them as chicks. Both of which I'm strongly against as a vegan.

  • Dairy cows - Again, no. Cows need to be post-pregnancy to produce milk. Much like humans and other mammals. The milk in the cow's udders is for it's calf. Every drop you take is every drop the calf doesn't get. But you could argue - "What if the calf has had enough and is almost completely off milk?" to that I say sure. Knock yourself out, but it's not a lot of milk. So again, not profitable. It's just something people do when they raise cows not-for-business. As pets. It's leftovers. If you want to make a business out of that and make the cow produce milk year-round, you'll have to impregnate her every year. That's abuse. Then there's also the concern about male calves. What do you do with them? One out of two chance you'll get a new male calf. Those are useless unless you're gonna slaughter them for meat. Either way, I don't see how it could be done humanely.

  • Lab grown meat - Yes. While I myself will probably eat very little of it because I don't find it appealing anymore, I do recognize other people's cravings for meat and a cruelty free solution is the best one. I also heard it could eventually be very cheap to mass-produce and would only require a small sample from the cow every few months.
